wave_title: Control Flow -- materialize the CONTROL_FLOW dimension (.atlas/contracts/SEMANTIC-FACTS.md#controlflowfact): ControlFlowBlockKind + ControlFlowEdgeKind + ControlFlowBlockIdentity typed kernel, and a real structured-CFG lowering pass for Rust function/method bodies computing actual successor edges (branches, loop repeats/skip edges, return/break/continue/panic terminators, labeled-break resolution through nested loops), not a placeholder. Unlike R4.5's CALL dimension, CFG structure is fully determined by Rust's own syntax/language semantics rather than requiring name/type resolution, so edges are computed for real; ControlFlowEdgeKind::Unresolved is reserved for genuinely ambiguous cases (an unmatched labeled break/continue).

cfg_model.kernel: core/src/semantic/control_flow.rs: ControlFlowBlockKind (FunctionEntry/IfThen/IfElse/LoopBody/WhileBody/ForLoopBody/MatchArm/NestedBlockExpr/Continuation -- structural role), ControlFlowEdgeKind (Fallthrough/Branch/LoopRepeat/Return/Break/Panic/Unresolved -- the contract's exact required categories: blocks, terminators, successors, exceptional/unwind edges, entry/exit), ControlFlowEdge { kind, target: Option<SemanticRecordId> }, ControlFlowBlockIdentity { repository, revision, function, block_index, kind, is_entry, successors }.
cfg_model.identity_key_design: ControlFlowBlockIdentity::identity_key() covers only repository/revision/function/block_index -- kind/is_entry/successors are content, not identity, for the same reason R4.5's CallSiteIdentity excludes dispatch/callees: block_index (assigned deterministically per function) already disambiguates identity, so record_id stays stable if a later wave computes a more precise successor set for the same block.
cfg_model.key_design_difference_from_call: Unlike R4.5's CALL dimension (where callee resolution genuinely requires name/type information this extractor doesn't have and never will), a function's control-flow STRUCTURE is fully determined by Rust's own syntax and language semantics, not by type inference or import resolution. There is therefore no equivalent epistemic reason to leave CFG edges unresolved by default -- real successor edges are computed wherever source syntax structurally determines them; ControlFlowEdgeKind::Unresolved is reserved for genuinely ambiguous cases (a labeled break/continue whose label matches no loop this extractor tracked).
cfg_model.extraction: adapter/src/semantic/rust/cfg.rs (new file): a real structured-CFG lowering pass. lower_stmts recursively splits a function body's statement list into blocks at branch/loop/early-exit boundaries; a Continuation enum (FallthroughTo/Return/LoopRepeat) threads 'what happens when this segment completes' through the recursion so join points and loop back-edges compose correctly across nesting; a loop_stack: Vec<LoopFrame> resolves labeled and unlabeled break/continue to the correct enclosing loop, walking innermost-to-outermost past intermediate unlabeled loops to find a matching label. while/for loops get a genuine 'may not enter' skip edge (the condition/iterator can be false/empty on the first check); a bare loop does not (always executes at least once). An else-if chain flattens into one multi-branch decision point rather than a synthetic intermediate node, consistent with the top-level if's own condition also never being modeled as a node. panic!/unreachable!/todo!/unimplemented! (matched via the macro path's last segment, so both bare and qualified invocations are caught, and both syn::Stmt::Macro and syn::Stmt::Expr(Expr::Macro(_), _) shapes) produce a Panic edge.
cfg_model.scope_this_wave: Only statement-level control flow is split into blocks: a construct nested inside a larger expression (e.g. `let x = if c {1} else {2};`) is not modeled -- its branches are still walked for CALL purposes (R4.5) but contribute no separate ControlFlow block/edge structure. Closures get no CFG of their own (build_control_flow is called exactly once per function/method body, never recursively for a nested closure). Both are documented gaps in the module doc comments, not silent omissions -- independently confirmed true of the code (not just asserted) by the independent verification pass.
cfg_model.graph_projection: core/src/graph/engineering_graph.rs: the previously no-op SemanticObservation::ControlFlow arm now creates one ControlFlowBlock node per block observation plus a HAS_BLOCK edge from the owning function's FunctionIdentity node (present for every block, not only the entry, so every block belonging to a function is discoverable without scanning record_ids), and one graph edge per successor whose target is concrete (Some). Successors with target=None (Return/Panic/Unresolved) correctly produce no graph edge -- they remain visible as block content/evidence, never silently dropped and never fabricated as a dangling edge.

still_unsupported: Expression-level CFG splitting -- a construct nested inside a larger expression (e.g. `let x = if c {1} else {2};`) is not modeled as its own blocks this wave; deferred, documented gap, not silently omitted.
Closures get no CFG of their own -- they have no FunctionIdentity in Atlas's model to attribute one to; independently confirmed via code trace, not just doc-comment assertion.

Try (`?`) propagation is not modeled as a distinct branching edge -- a block containing `?` is treated as ordinary Fallthrough content, matching the conservative documented-gap pattern from prior waves.
DATA_FLOW / STATE / EFFECT / OWNERSHIP / CONCURRENCY / PERSISTENCE -- unmaterialized, unchanged from R4.5.

Cross-function/interprocedural CFG traversal, reachability, or cycle detection -- this wave only records individual functions' own CFGs; no graph algorithm consumes the HAS_BLOCK/successor edges yet beyond their existence.
Full compiler/global Rust name resolution -- unchanged; CFG structure computation never required it, but CALL resolution still doesn't have it either.
